text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leaders of world's leading industrial nations, while welcoming signs of improving global economy, say more needs to be done to ensure good times continue and everyone benefits.
- Fifty-four percent of Hong Kong residents believe China will become more like Hong Kong in 25 years, as compared with 18 percent who think it will be other way around, according to Time/CNN poll.
- Thousands of Filipino maids worry Chinese women from mainland will take their jobs at much lower wages after territory handed over to China at end of month.
- Taiwanese president Lee Teng-hui is to inspect troops during two-day war games, a move almost sure to infuriate Beijing despite downplaying of games by Taiwan military.
- Singapore Telecom may be forced to offer its own version of callback services if pushed to wall by competition.

- Most of Thailands once high-flying banks expected to report double-digit falls in earnings this year as they are forced to make provisions to cover sour loans to ailing property sector, analysts say.

- Group of Seven (G7) summit's economic talks offered no new factors to rattle major currency markets, which will continue to be overshadowed by intensifying U.S.-Japan trade tensions and lingering uncertainty over European single currency, senior traders say.

- Prime Stevens/Balmoral Roads area could see at least half a dozen more collective sales, including large 94,000 sq ft site owned by Indian High Commission, before tap dries up on this market segment.
- Far East Organization's Bishan 8 sets record selling prices for leasehold condominiums over weekend, with units sold fetching prices that averaged Singapore $1,100 per sq ft.

- U.S. dollar expected to rise significantly against yen this week now that Washington has balked at idea of using exchange rates as weapon to slash Japan's ballooning trade surpluses duing weekend G7 summit in Denver.
- Goldtron Ltd has again made no provisions for Malaysian $132.9 million lawsuit because matter remains at early stage of arbitration.
- Year after its takeover by Salim Group, breadmaker QAF pushing ahead with plans to repeat success of its Gardenia line in region.
